comment: I did not think I would do well in calculus, but I ended with an A and owe all the credit to Mrs. Brooks. Classes are lecture heavy, but she explains concepts with many practice problems. She is very helpful outside class with many office hours and optional homework for extra credit. Tests and quizzes are manageable if you put in the effort always.

Kay Brooks is a fine enough teacher, but her grading is HARSH. She will literally find anything to take off for, and if your work isn't exactly like something you'd see worked in a textbook, your grade will suffer. She genuinely took off a point because my GRAMMAR was bad and 1 because I drew --> instead of = to the next step.

This professor was extremely clear and went very slow. The first month and half is literally just pre-calc review. She is very sweet and her tests are fair. She is a little bit meticulous when it come to grading, but once you start understand her system you will be fine. Also, if you do higher on the final than one of ur tests the final replaces it

If you have to take calc she's probably your best choice. Not the best at teaching the material but tests are not intended to trick you. Do the homework, understand it, & you'll be fine. Unlike the other calc professors she does a month of review of basic precalc.If you know this already then you will basically get a few easy A's to start out with

I've had Professor Brooks twice, and I would 100% take her again if she taught upper-level classes. She is a little picky on grading, but if you show your work like her in-class examples, you'll do well. Exams are super easy, and you get 2 attempts on your homework. The third exam was the only one I even studied for. Super easy A.

So far from intellectually stimulating, fortunately the content is pretty easy, but its just such a drag taking it with Brooks. If you have the opportunity to take it with someone else, do it. I think my understanding of calc got worse while taking her class.

Good professor and explains concepts well but goes through the material very fast. You can get extra credit from doing all of the assigned homework. Class expectations are made very clear with daily class recaps posted on Blackboard. Meticulous grader which can be annoying at times. Extra practice worksheets were uploaded online for some concepts

Professor Brooks was a great teacher who was very detailed and organized. She constantly sent out updates and was clear on what she expected. As I had already taken calculus in high school, I found her class to be a light review and not time-consuming. What's nice is that she offers extra credit just by doing the homework which is amazing.

She is a good calc professor, but she does go through content quickly. Also, you will find that the content that we learn in class is much easier than what she tests you on in exams. But she helps with extra credit for exams if you do all the homework. She is also great in office hours. This class was hard for me with little prior calc knowledge.

Honestly Dr. Brooks is amazing at explaining calculus in such a clear and concise way. Things tend to pick up speed around half-way through the semester, so I would definitely recommend to not skip out on lectures or breeze past the example problems/homework. Very meticulous in her grading, so be very careful in writing down your steps.

I took an unrelated class here once where the professor didn't even know the content themselves. I got a higher grade in that class than I did here. Turned in the final exam all confident and it comes back leagues below an F. Just don't.
She is so helpful and nice, but a bit of a tough grader.

Not a bad course! If you're lost, you have unambiguous materials to help you learn. But I implore you, if you're a bad test taker, pick someone else. Homework is optional and counts for extra points on a test, but in the best case, the extra points are negligible. Most of the graded work is quizzes and tests, but feedback is only sometimes unclear.
this is going to be a hard class if your not good at math. i would NOT recommend
She is a super nice and kind person. Just go to the lectures and take the classes carefully, you will be fine. Take her lecture, it worths!

Super nice, lectures for all of the class. If you pay attention and take notes you probably don't need to read the textbook. Questions on quizzes and tests usually aren't too complicated so they aren't too difficult, especially if you do the optional homework.
Her class is extremely lecture heavy, but she is very nice and everything is relatively straight forward.

This is a good class. She is a nice person who is accessible outside of class, but it is hard to get your questions answered while she is lecturing. It's a very lecture heavy class, but the tests and homework are reasonable. She is VERY particular on 'showing your work' and will take off points until you figure out how she likes to see it.

Professor Brooks lectures for the entire class. She sometimes makes mistakes while teaching and writes on the whiteboard by writing theorems with one or two examples each section. This class is very fast and she sometimes goes over time. There are 3 tests and a final.
